players.note: That's four straight games with fewer than four yards per attempt for D'Andre Swift. You'd think that with Kyle Monangai out, he would be crushing it, but you'd be wrong. I'm ready to jump ship before it's too late
Volume monster, but he has a brutal schedule ahead, and Dallas still hasn't had their bye week. He's still a top-12 RB for the rest of the season, but an RB6 ECR is too high for me.

Brutal run-out for Chase Brown. He hasn't had more than 13 carries in a game since Week 2. The lack of touchdown volume is really killing him right now. Surely he'll get lucky and stumble into the end zone once or twice shortly. That's when you sell.

Jaboy Brissett is here to save the day! The ceiling isn't quite as high without Lamar, but he's the only real target in this offense, and we've seen Brissett sling it before. At high-end WR2 prices, Zay is a hold.

Week 9 wasn't very efficient for Tuten, but they also didn't need him against a Joe Fagnano-led offense. He's still an RB1 on one of the NFL's best offenses. But low if anyone is worried about last week's usage.
Nico Collins' target rate this season: 20.2%. Not great. C.J. Stroud spreads it out to much for Collins to be a jam every week; especially with Tank Dell healthy now.

Pickens saw his snap share reduce throughout the season, seemingly getting passed up on the depth chart by Ryan Flournoy. Now, we all know Pickens is the superior talent, but something is going on here. I'm holding and praying for a trade, or for these to return to normal in regard to the pecking order in Dallas.

Jonah Coleman has led the backfield by a healthy margin, logging 56% of carries over the past two weeks. Second is J.K. Dobbins, at 22%. Jonah Coleman is the trusted bell cow to close out the season; invest in him now!

I get it. Nearly every other running back is injured or sucks. Who's left to choose from? However, I think the real Tony Pollard is much closer to the version we saw in Weeks 1-6, rather than the one we saw in Weeks 7-8. If Pollard is the guy who beats me, so be it.

Rashee Rice has led this team with a 22% target share over the past two weeks. While that's not a tremendous number, it's worth noting that Xavier Worthy suffered a hamstring injury in Week 9. If he misses any time, it's just down to Rice, Kelce, and Walker.

In my opinion, an RB14 ECR is too conservative. With Jacoby at quarterback now, this offense has some theoretical life again. Henry has great upcoming matchups against LAC and CAR and could carry you to some big wins in the latter half of the season.

Evans is trending toward missing Week 10, too. At this point, I'm tired of this song and dance. Evans can't stay healthy, and you don't want this to be the guy you rely on in the fantasy playoffs. Time to move on.
Kittle performed poorly in a smash spot against the Raiders without Mike Evans. It was disappointing, but no need to panic. He's still a top-tier TE option for the rest of the season.

Diggs is another guy who is totally fine, but a bit overpriced as a high-end WR3. He's only surpassed five receptions in a game once this season. He has a decent floor, but the ceiling isn't exciting. Since he doesn't provide much value over replacement, I'd rather take a swing on a rookie or an ascending asset.
As expected, Breece came in and immediately became the 1A in this backfield again. He's a tier below some of these other workhorses, but is a clear buy at low RB2 prices.

Another poor week from Quinshon. He's posted back-to-back duds, and the volume has dipped a hair since Sampson returned. If you're going to sell, wait for a bounceback game where he finds the end zone (or after their Week 11 bye) to maximize returns.

AJB could return in Week 10. More than likely, he'll return after their Week 11 bye. If you're in a great spot and can afford to keep him on your bench, AJB is a great target. Romeo Doubs has no clear timetable for return, and Brown should (in theory) dominate the target share once he returns.
Third receiving option on his own team. Sure, he got there in Week 9 with his first touchdown on the season, but he's also only surpassed four receptions in a game once this year.

My goodness, is this kid ever going to play a full game? The injuries keep stacking up, as do the losses for Los Angeles. No reason to sell now; you won't get anything for Ladd. Just keep him stashed on the bench and pray.

Apparent Baker is total dust, and all of his receivers are irrelevant as a product. But with Egbuka coming off a down week and headed into the bye, you'd only get pennies on the dollar right now. I'm waiting for Week 11 against Detroit, who has been known to give up plenty of passing production. Feel free to sell high if he has a big game then.

Omar Cooper got back on track in Week 9, catching eight of nine targets. The one big caveat is that Garrett Wilson was hurt. But I'm comfortable buying at WR36 prices, and I'm pretty confident in saying Cooper is the WR2 over Adonai Mitchell.

Hey, we got Tyson back! Outside of a costly fumble in scoring position, I thought he looked great in his NFL debut. Tyson had four targets on 16 routes, which is a 25% target rate. Assuming New Orleans slowly ramps him up to a full-time role, Tyson could be a must-start asset in a couple of weeks.

Unfortunately, the breakout hasn't quite happened yet, but the target volume is slowly trending in the right direction. Don't drop Williams yet; he has a great schedule to end the fantasy regular season to into the playoffs, and could be peaking around that time.

Kraft is a fine asset; he's just overpriced as the TE7 on ECR. He's multiple tiers below Christian Watson and Matthew Golden and the clear third option on his team. Yes, GB throws it a ton, making him relevant enough. I'd just prefer to cash out at the price.

Another 7-target game for Tyler Warren. Unfortunately, Daniel Jones is such a pathetic quarterback that it doesn't matter much. We're looking at a high-floor, low-ceiling play with Warren. I'm holding for now.

He's not exciting, but he's running every route for the Chiefs, and the WR group has been banged up all season. He provides a safe floor and just needs to find the end zone a few times to really pay off.

Mayer was close to a big game in Week 9, but he fumbled at the goal line. Target volume is a bit volatile, but as the ECR TE21, I think that's already baked in. I'm happy to have Mayer as my TE2 for injuries or bye weeks.
